body.p: REMARKS
This response is in reply to the Non-Final Office Action dated March 22, 2024 (hereinafter the "Action"). Reconsideration is respectfully requested.
Status of Claims

Claims 1-19 were pending. Claims 1, 3, 4, 6-7, 11-14, 16, and 19 are amended herein. Claim 20 is new. Support for the claim amendments and new claim can be found throughout the specification and drawings and at least at paragraphs [0240] to [0250].

Applicant would like to thank the Examiner for indicating claim 12 is objected to as being dependent upon a rejected base claim, but would be allowable if rewritten in independent form including all of the limitations of the base claim and any intervening claims. Claims 1-11 and 13-19 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over US10,354,460 to Ricci (hereinafter "Ricci").
The Traversal
Applicant traverses the rejections, contending that the cited references fail to meet the requirements necessary to establish a prima facie case of obviousness.
Amended claim 1 recites:
A computer-implemented method comprising the
operations of:
obtaining vehicle dimension data describing dimensions of
a vehicle;
causing, based at least in part on the vehicle dimension
data, a robotic apparatus to move to a first position about the
vehicle to collect data regarding a selected wheel of the vehicle;
determining a first reference point of the vehicle based at
least in part on the collected data regarding the selected wheel;
and
causing the robotic apparatus to move to a second position
about the vehicle based on the determined first reference point.
Applicant respectfully asserts Ricci fails to disclose the claimed operations.
First, the Office Action alleges Ricci teaches "obtaining a vehicle

dimension data describing dimensions of a vehicle" citing "Fig. 2, 4A, 4B and 6-12 element 100." Applicant is unclear how the Action is suggesting the cited figures and element 100 teach this step, because the figures merely show a diagram (not a method) including a vehicle. Applicant respectfully submits the figures do not show "obtaining vehicle dimension data describing dimensions of a vehicle." Further, the specification is completely silent with respect to obtaining vehicle dimension data describing dimensions of a vehicle. It is clear the reference does not explicitly disclose "obtaining vehicle dimension data describing dimensions of a vehicle." Further this step of the operation is not inherent simply by obtaining a vehicle. Therefore, Ricci fails to disclose "obtaining vehicle dimension data describing dimensions of a vehicle."
Ricci also fails to disclose "causing, based at least in part on the

vehicle dimension data, a robotic apparatus to move to a first position about the vehicle to collect data regarding a selected wheel of the vehicle." The Office Action alleges Ricci teaches moving a robotic apparatus to a first position about the vehicle. (Action at 5). However, the alleged robotic apparatus, robotic unit 700 in Ricci, does not move based on vehicle dimension data and the robotic unit 700 does not move to a first position about the vehicle to collect data regarding a selected wheel of the vehicle. The only movement of the robotic unit 700 in Ricci is to "manoeuver charging plate 520 relative to charging panel 608 of vehicle 100." (Ricci at 7:1-2). Therefore, Ricci also fails to disclose "causing, based at least in part on the vehicle dimension data, a robotic apparatus to move to a first position about the vehicle to collect data regarding a selected wheel of the vehicle."

Ricci fails to disclose "determining a first reference point of the vehicle based at least in part on the collected data regarding the selected wheel." The robotic unit 700 in Ricci does not determine a first reference point of the vehicle based at least in part on the collected data regarding the selected wheel. Instead, the robotic unit 700 maneuvers the charging plate 520 to a position relative to the charging panel 608. Thus, the alleged first reference point in Ricci is the charging panel 608, which is not determined on collected data regarding the selected wheel. Therefore, Ricci also fails to disclose "determining a first reference point of the vehicle based at least in part on the collected data regarding the selected wheel."
Ricci fails to disclose "causing the robotic apparatus to move to a
second position about the vehicle based on the determined first reference

point." As there is no first reference point based at least in part on the collect, the robotic unit 700 in Ricci cannot teach moving the robotic unit 700 to a second point based on the first reference. Therefore, Ricci does not disclose "causing the robotic apparatus to move to a second position about the vehicle based on the determined first reference point."

The absence of these elements from Ricci marks a difference between the prior art and the claimed invention. To support a rejection on the basis of obviousness the Examiner is required to "explain why the differences between the prior art and the claimed invention would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art" (MPEP, section 2141, III) as well as provide "articulated reasoning with some rational underpinning to support the legal conclusion of obviousness" (KSR International Co. v. Teleflex Inc., 550 U.S. 398, 82 USPQ2d 1385, 1396 (2007)). Applicant contends that the Examiner has not addressed the aforementioned difference between Ricci and the claimed invention, i.e., the Examiner has not explained why the difference between the prior art and the claimed invention would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art, nor has the Examiner provided articulated reasoning with some rational underpinning to support the legal conclusion of obviousness. Therefore, the requirements to establish a prima facie case of obviousness for claim 1 have not been met. Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection of claim 1 be withdrawn.

Applicant respectfully asserts many of the citations in the rejection to Ricci only include figures and element reference numbers. However, the cited figures do not illustrate a method and the element reference numbers are not to a step of a method. Without further explanation, it is unclear to the Applicant how the cited figures and element disclose the claimed steps.
If the rejection is maintained, the Applicant respectfully request clarification as to how the cited figures and elements teach the claimed method.
Claim 14
Although not identical, claim 14 includes similar features to those recited in claim 1. Claim 14 comprises a processor configured to perform operations comprising:
obtaining vehicle dimension data describing
dimensions of a vehicle;
causing, based at least in part on the vehicle
dimension data, the robotic apparatus to move to a first position about the vehicle to collect data regarding a selected wheel of the
vehicle;
determining a first reference point of the vehicle
based at least in part on the collected data regarding the selected
wheel; and
causing the robotic apparatus to move to a second
position about the vehicle based on the determined first reference
point.
Therefore, claim 14 is patentable over Ricci for at least the same reasons as claim 1. Applicant respectfully requests the withdrawal of the rejection of claim 14 as unpatentable over Ricci.

Claims 2-11, 13, 15-19 are rejected as obvious over Ricci. However, these claims depend from claim 1 or claim 14, and thus include all of the recitations of claim 1 or claim 14. Therefore, claims 2-11, 13, and 15-19 are

patentable over Ricci for at least the same reasons as claim 1 and claim 14. It is well established that if an independent claim is nonobvious under 35 USC 103, then any claim depending therefrom is nonobvious. In re Fine, 5 USPQ2d, 1596 (Fed. Cir. 1988). Applicant requests that the rejection of claims 2-11, 13, and 15-19 as unpatentable over Ricci be withdrawn.

New claim 21 includes the subject matter of originally filed claim 1 and the allowable subject matter of claim 12 along with the subject matter of intervening claims 10 and 11. Therefore, Applicant contends new claim 21 is allowable over the cited references.
Summary

Applicant has shown that the cited references fail to meet the standard for obviousness. Applicant contends that the claims, as amended, are therefore allowable over the cited references and requests that all rejections be withdrawn. Applicant further requests the application passed to issue. An early and favorable decision is earnestly solicited.
